case_name: State of Rajasthan v Mohammad Muslim Tagala
respondent:
Mohammad Muslim Tagala
Supreme Court of India

13 October 2014
Cr.A. No. 2184 of 2014 [Arising out of S.L.P. (Cr.) No. 5192 of 2014]
The Judgment was delivered by : Ranjana Prakash Desai, J.
1. Leave granted.
2. The respondent was tried along with two
facts: The respondent was tried along with two others viz. Sabena and Mohd. Daud by the Additional District & Sessions Judge (Fast Track), Sikkar, Rajasthan in Sessions Case No.24 of 2007 for offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376, 307 read with S.109 of the Indian Penal Code ('the IPC').
Learned Sessions Judge, Sikkar by judgment and order dated 11/6/2008 acquitted Sabena and Mohd. Daud, of all the charges.
The respondent was convicted for offence punishable u/s.363 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for three years and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default, to undergo SI for six months.
He was also convicted under Section 366A of the IPC and sentenced to suffer RI for five years and to pay a fine of Rs.2,000/-, in default, to undergo SI for six months.
He was also convicted for offence punishable u/s.376 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for seven years and to pay fine of Rs.5,000/-, in default, to undergo SI for six months.
issues: Whether the High Court erred in giving a direction to the State Government to commute the sentence of the respondent.
Whether the Public Prosecutor's concession was proper in the circumstances.
petitioner_arguments: The offence committed by the respondent was grave and, therefore, the High Court erred in giving a direction to the authorities to give benefit of S.433 of the Code to the respondent.
The Public Prosecutor did not oppose the request made by the respondent's counsel that the concerned authorities be directed to give the benefit of S.433 of the Code to the respondent.
respondent_arguments: The respondent has undergone seven years' imprisonment and has been released from custody.
The High Court gave a direction to the concerned authorities to give the appellant benefit of S.433 of the Code and disposed of the appeal.
court_reasoning: S.433 of the Code pertains to power of the appropriate Government to commute the sentence without the consent of the person sentenced.
The court cannot direct the appropriate Government to exercise its sovereign powers.
The Court can merely give a direction to the appropriate Government to consider the case for commutation of sentence and nothing more.
holding: The appeal is disposed of as infructuous.
